title: Thirty-two countries founded the Organisation of African Unity
body: On 25 May 1963, representatives of 32 independent African states met in Addis Ababa, Ethiopia, and established the Organisation of African Unity. Its successor, the African Union, held its first summit in Durban in 2002.
takeaway: An institution can expand its membership and change its structure as the states that formed it change.
source: African Union, Member States and Assembly Decisions
visual: delegates around a conference table in a mid-century hall in Addis Ababa

title: US senators were once chosen by state legislatures
body: The original US Constitution assigned the choice of senators to state legislatures. The 17th Amendment, ratified in 1913, transferred that choice to voters in each state while keeping two senators per state.
takeaway: Who chooses a representative can change even if the offices and their geographical allocation stay the same.
source: Constitution Annotated, United States Congress, Seventeenth Amendment
visual: a small ballot box on the table of an early twentieth-century polling place
